1 Strategic Intent
What Trident is trying to achieve - and what it is not trying to achieve.
Trident's aim is not to become the school that uses the greatest number of AI tools. The aim is to become a school that uses AI
intelligently, selectively and safely to improve the quality of learning, teaching, leadership and school operations while
deliberately protecting the human relationships, judgement, character and community at the heart of the College.

content:
TRIDENT AI STRATEGIC PROJECT PLAN 2026 2029 FINAL - STRATEGIC PROPOSITION:
AI is an enabling layer across the school, not a separate technology project. Every initiative must
begin with an educational or organisational problem worth solving.
The project will pursue five strategic outcomes
• Learning: more responsive, personalised and intellectually demanding learning, with students remaining active thinkers rather
than passive recipients of generated answers.
• Teachers: lower avoidable workload, stronger planning and assessment, and faster access to curriculum information and insight
- including syllabus requirements, curriculum sequencing, student misconceptions, assessment evidence and appropriate
teaching resources - giving teachers more time for relationships, feedback and professional judgement.
• Leadership and operations: faster access to relevant school information, reduced duplication, better analysis and more efficient
routine processes.
• Community: clearer access to school information and improved support for students, staff, parents, admissions and governance.
• Human development and ethics: students and staff who understand AI capability, limitations, bias, privacy, verification,
authorship and responsible use.
Non-goals
• Replacing teachers, counsellors, leaders or safeguarding professionals with automated decision-making.
• Deploying student-facing AI simply because it is novel or commercially attractive.
• Uploading confidential or sensitive school information into unapproved public AI services.

Principle Operational meaning
Human first AI supports human judgement; accountability remains with people.
Educational purpose Every deployment must solve a defined learning, teaching or organisational problem.

Evidence before expansion Pilots are measured before school-wide adoption.
Capability, not dependency AI use should strengthen thinking, expertise and agency rather than weaken them.
The Trident LTCES Framework - developed by Trident College
Trident College has developed the LTCES Framework as a practical internal decision tool to ensure that every significant AI
initiative is educationally worthwhile, supportive of people, appropriate for the community, ethically responsible and
sustainable. Before a material AI initiative is approved, the Steering Group should explicitly test it against the five dimensions
below. Failure against the ethical or safeguarding dimension should stop the initiative; weakness in any other dimension should
trigger redesign before scale.

Trident should favour a controlled ecosystem over a proliferation of disconnected consumer tools. The existing Microsoft 365
environment should form the default identity, document, collaboration and permissions layer wherever practical,
supplemented only by approved tools that meet educational, privacy, safeguarding, integration and value requirements.
Target architecture
• Identity and access: school-managed accounts, role-based permissions and appropriate age controls.
• Approved AI layer: secure institutional AI tools rather than unmanaged personal accounts for school data.
• Knowledge layer: curated policies, curriculum resources, handbooks, templates and approved internal information with clear
ownership and version control.
• Agent layer: specialised assistants for defined tasks, each constrained to approved information, prompts, workflows and permissions.
• Human oversight: no autonomous high-stakes decision-making; professional review remains explicit.
• Monitoring layer: adoption, incidents, costs, feedback, performance and quality measures.

5 People, Pedagogy and Capability
The project succeeds only if staff confidence, professional judgement and educational design develop faster than tool
adoption. Staff development should therefore be practical, differentiated and linked to real work rather than generic “prompt
training”.
Capability stage Expected capability Audience
Level 1 - Awareness Understand generative AI, limitations, hallucinations, bias, privacy and Trident rules. All staff
Level 2 - Confidence Use approved AI safely for routine professional tasks and verify outputs. All staff
Level 3 - Pedagogical integration Redesign learning, questioning, feedback and assessment around purposeful AI use. Teaching staff
Level 4 - Innovation Design repeatable workflows, agents, shared resources and evaluation approaches. AI Champions / selected leaders
Professional learning model
• Short whole-staff foundations followed by role-specific workshops and department application.
• “Bring a real task” sessions: teachers use AI on an actual lesson, assessment, report, data set or resource and compare quality
and time saved.
• Department exemplars: each department identifies high-value and high-risk uses relevant to its subject.
• Peer observation and sharing: AI Champions collect strong examples, examples of where AI has not worked well, and real-life
situations where the appropriate use of AI is unclear and requires professional judgement.

Student access to AI must be paired with explicit instruction. The goal is not merely competent tool use; it is disciplined

13 End-State: What “AI-Enabled Trident” Should Mean by 2029
By 2029, success should not look like a school saturated with visible AI products. It should look like a school in which useful AI
capability has become a secure, governed and largely unobtrusive layer underneath excellent human practice.
Area 2029 end-state
Students
Can use AI critically and ethically, verify information, disclose assistance, protect their own thinking and demonstrate
authentic understanding.
Teachers
Have increased pedagogical understanding and professional confidence, with reliable AI support for selected high-value
work that strengthens planning, assessment and feedback while retaining curriculum authority, judgement, relationships
and subject expertise.
Leaders
Can retrieve and synthesise approved information more efficiently and have stronger decision support without delegating
accountability to algorithms.
School systems
Use a smaller number of well-governed tools and agents, with clear ownership, permissions, data standards, evidence
and retirement rules.
Community
Understands why Trident uses AI, what the school protects, and how responsible AI use supports rather than diminishes a
holistic education.
Board
Can see evidence of educational value, workforce capability, organisational benefit, cost control and responsible risk
management.
